title: Variability-driven batching probe for mixed-workload throughput & p95 regression
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build and run a harness that emphasizes variability-driven batching and queueing artifacts across realistic mixed tenant workloads, and produce signal-rich metrics for tokens/sec and tail latency (p95/p99) so regression detection is reliable.

Scope:
- Synthesize arrival streams (Poisson baseline, heavy-tailed bursts, scheduled bimodal peaks, and per-tenant diurnal skew).
- Exercise the continuous batching runtime with adjustable batching window, max batch size, and adaptive throttling knobs.
- Toggle KV prefix caching and cold/warm cache scenarios.
- Collect token/sec, p95/p99 latency, batch size distribution, queue length, GPU utilization, and per-tenant fairness variance.

Success criteria:
- Instrumented harness that reproduces p95 regressions observed in production microbursts.
- Regression detector that flags >15% sustained p95 increase or 25% decrease in tokens/sec over baseline with <5% false positive rate on synthetic benign replays.
- Actionable recommendations for batching window defaults and a guardrail for autoscaler thresholds.
results_summary: Initial runs (run-id: vdb-2026-03-04) show: baseline steady-state tokens/sec = 128k +/- 4% (95% CI), baseline p95 = 42ms. Under bimodal microburst profile (30s bursts at 3x arrival rate) p95 jumps to 210ms (400% increase) when batching window is fixed at 20ms. Adaptive-window policy reduced p95 to 85ms while preserving 87% of baseline tokens/sec. Enabling KV prefix caching for warm sessions reduced mean batch size by 12% and lowered p95 variance by 18%. Regression detector using EWMA + control chart detected the injected 30% p95 regression within 2 sampling windows with one false positive during an extreme heavy-tail run. Full data and chart artifacts: drive link below.

analysis_notes: Trade-offs observed: larger fixed windows yield higher throughput but amplify tail latency during short high-rate bursts. Adaptive-window reduces tail but may slightly reduce aggregate tokens/sec during sustained steady high concurrency due to smaller effective batch sizes. KV caching benefits tail variance but hides cold-start behaviors; recommend separate cold/warm baseline runs for alert calibration. Autoscaler thresholds interact with batching: aggressive scale-up reduces queueing but may fragment batches, reducing per-GPU efficiency.
recommendations: Ship adaptive-window (initial heuristic: base_window=8ms, max_window=50ms, growth_backoff=1.5x) as opt-in runtime flag for mixed-tenant clusters.
Add 'cold-session' mode to harness to calibrate cold cache p95 baselines and ensure regression detector includes cold/warm labeling.
Expose per-tenant p95 breakdown in console and wire regression alerts to route to runtime-oncall with severity metadata.
Run extended 48h soak in staging with representative tenant mix and record false positive/negative rates for the detector before enabling in prod.
